note: Two lists, drafted at 1.7 from the coverage measurement recorded in PROGRESS.md. They govern the theme and company searches the research pass makes against the open web. They do not govern the licensed news feed: that feed delivers 1173 of 1253 measured articles under one domain, and the domain is the aggregator rather than the writing outlet, so a domain filter over it would discard everything or nothing. Admissibility is judged per document after the fetch in both cases. (see: Two source lists govern the open web, and the licensed feed is a channel rather than a list)

companyNews.purpose: reporting about a named company: results, guidance, management, transactions
companyNews.gatedNote: Kept on the list and expected to return nothing to an automated fetch. They are listed so a later review measures whether that is still true rather than rediscovering the question, and so a search that surfaces them is not silently narrowed. (see: Gated sources are out of scope, and access is ranked before reputation)

industry.purpose: theme material: what an industry is doing, independent of any one company's quarter
industry.gatedNote: Measured at 6.9 by a search that ran, one a site over the quarter to 2026-09-08 for an industry the site covers. Kept on the list and expected to return nothing to an automated fetch: ihsmarkit.com returned no result. The two other sites marked here until then were guesses the search contradicted: statista.com returned ten pages of ten with their text and a publish date, and digitimes.com three of ten, the other seven arriving as snippets.

reviewNote: Reviewed at 6.0 against the coverage measurement 1.7 took, and the review's finding is what the measurement can and cannot settle. It cannot review either list by domain: it measured the licensed news feed, which these lists do not govern, and that feed carried 1,173 of 1,253 articles under one domain because the domain in the payload is the aggregator rather than the writing outlet. So no entry is added or removed on its evidence, and doing so would be tuning a search list on a feed. What it does settle is recorded here. The three writing outlets it observed inside the article text, Business Wire, Globe Newswire and Bloomberg, are all on the company-news list already. Every one of the 1,253 articles carried retrievable text, so the document a claim rests on arrives with the feed row and the unretrievable-text case admissibility must refuse is a search-tool case rather than a feed case. And coverage thins by about four to one from the top of the index to the bottom, 883 articles for the top third against 175 for the bottom over the same fortnight with one name of thirty drawing none, which says that the bottom of the index has material for a per-name pass and not much of it. The industry list still has no evidence behind it at all, which 1.7 named and this review confirms rather than repairs: nothing can measure it until a search runs against it.
industryMeasuredNote: What the 6.9 search returned from each site, storable meaning on the site with text longer than its snippet and a publish date: semiconductors.org 10 of 10, trendforce.com 10 of 10, statista.com 10 of 10, iea.org 9 of 10, worldsteel.org 5 of 7, digitimes.com 3 of 10, spglobal.com 2 of 10, eia.gov 1 of 1, and no result from bls.gov, census.gov, federalreserve.gov or ihsmarkit.com. So eight of the twelve return a page whose text can be stored. The same theme search restricted to the whole list for the fixture's four industries, Consumer Electronics, Scientific & Technical Instruments, Software - Infrastructure and Entertainment, returned nothing, and that is a measure of the search rather than of the list: Consumer Electronics is the industry statista.com was searched for alone, a minute after the whole list drew nothing for it, and its ten of ten above say that a search over the whole list can return nothing for an industry a site on it covers. At 6.11 the whole list returned nothing for all four of those industries and for Semiconductors, while each site searched alone returned pages from five to nine of the twelve for each industry, so a theme pass searches each site alone. Over those searches worldsteel.org and ihsmarkit.com returned no page with text for any of the four, and a single-site search for worldsteel.org once answered with three pages from other sites. In 6.11's production runs over the fixture's night, a theme pass for each of those four industries, searching a site at a time, stored 29, 15, 14 and 8 pages for Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, Entertainment and Scientific & Technical Instruments, and its call wrote an accepted cycle for all four, two of them on the second draft; a run begun twenty-four minutes earlier stored 23, 18, 11 and 6, and the research model answered with nothing for Software - Infrastructure and Scientific & Technical Instruments, so whether a theme's cycle is written moves between two runs of the same pass. The pages those four cycles were handed came from bls.gov, census.gov, federalreserve.gov, spglobal.com, statista.com, trendforce.com, digitimes.com, iea.org and semiconductors.org, and none from eia.gov, worldsteel.org or ihsmarkit.com.
